title: Protocols for Preparation of Blood Films and Reporting of Malaria Parasites
author: Kwame Adusei
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.pq6dmze

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THICK SMEAR
steps.instruction: A drop of well mixed blood (6ul) was placed on a clean grease free slide using a pipette.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THICK SMEAR
steps.instruction: An applicator was used to spread the drop of blood in a circular way to ensure the spread of blood with moderate thickness, covering evenly an area about 1cm diameters.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THICK SMEAR
steps.instruction: Slides were labeled with subject’s code number and allowed to air-dry.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THICK SMEAR
steps.instruction: The smears were stained with a freshly prepared 10% Giemsa stain for 15 minutes and washed with clean distilled water.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THICK SMEAR
steps.instruction: The slides were then placed on a drying rack in a vertical position and allowed to air dry.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THIN SMEARS
steps.instruction: A drop of well mixed blood (2ul) was placed about 1cm from the frosted end of a slide using a pipette.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THIN SMEARS
steps.instruction: A smooth clean edge of a second slide (spreader) was placed on the specimen slide, just in front of the blood drop.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THIN SMEARS
steps.instruction: The spreader slide was held at 30° angle and was drawn back against the drop of blood.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THIN SMEARS
steps.instruction: As the blood started to spread to the ends of the spreader, the spreader was pushed forward with a light, smooth, and quick steady motion.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THIN SMEARS
steps.instruction: The frosted edge was labeled with the subject’s code number and the blood smear was dipped in a Coplin jar containing absolute methanol for 10 seconds and then air dried again.

steps.title: PREPARATION OF THIN SMEARS
steps.instruction: The smear was then stained with a freshly prepared Giemsa stain solution for 30 minutes and washed with distilled water

steps.title: Dry slides and examine under oil
steps.instruction: The slides were then placed on a drying rack and allowed to air dry. An oil immersion was put on the prepared thick film and was examined using the X100 objective lens and the thin films were first examined using the X40 with an oil immersion placed to the feathery tip of the smear to check the staining, morphology and distribution of the cells and afterwards the objective lens is changed to X100 to examine the malaria parasites.

substeps.instruction: Place slides on a drying rack and allow to air‑dry.
Add an oil immersion lens to the prepared thick film.
Examine the thick film using the 100× (X100) objective lens.
Examine thin films with the 40× (X40) objective, placing oil immersion at the feathery tip of the smear to check staining, morphology, and cell distribution.
Switch to the 100× (X100) objective to examine malaria parasites.

steps.title: •	REPORTING OF MALARIA PARASITES
steps.instruction: Number of parasites seen are counted in relation to a predetermined number of white blood cells and an average of 8000/µl is taken as standard. 200 white blood cells are counted in 100 fields. All parasite species and forms including both sexual and asexual forms are counted together.

steps.title: •	BLOOD SAMPLES PROCESSING FOR MALARIA DIAGNOSIS USING MALARIA RDT (HRP-2)
steps.instruction: In the laboratory, 5ul of whole blood from the labeled EDTA tube, was taken with a pipette provided with the test kit.

steps.title: •	BLOOD SAMPLES PROCESSING FOR MALARIA DIAGNOSIS USING MALARIA RDT (HRP-2)
steps.instruction: The blood was pipetted into the round sample well of the RDT.

steps.title: •	BLOOD SAMPLES PROCESSING FOR MALARIA DIAGNOSIS USING MALARIA RDT (HRP-2)
steps.instruction: Four drops of assay diluent were placed vertically into the square assay diluent well and the results were read after 30 minutes.

steps.title: •	BLOOD SAMPLES PROCESSING FOR MALARIA DIAGNOSIS USING MALARIA RDT (HRP-2)
steps.instruction: The same procedure was performed on samples collected from blood donors and non-donors.

steps.title: •	BLOOD SAMPLES PROCESSING FOR MALARIA DIAGNOSIS USING MALARIA RDT (HRP-2)
steps.instruction: A positive results was recorded when a pink/ red band appeared at the P. falciparum region and the test was reported as falciparum positive. A negative results was also recorded when only the control band shows.

steps.title: •	BLOOD GROUPING
steps.instruction: The tile method using the forward grouping was used for determining the blood groups of blood donors and non-donors (controls)

steps.title: •	QUESTIONNAIRE
steps.instruction: The questionnaire was categorized into a three-part document with a socio-demographics section, knowledge section and a section on attitudes and practices. Responses to a total of 20 opened and closed complete questions were unspecified so as to obtain validated answers without fear of victimization. Health workers were given less than 24hours to fill the questionnaire and those who did not submit were followed up in person

steps.title: •	BLOOD GROUPING
steps.instruction: 5ul of blood donors and non-donors blood samples were put in the appropriate square of the tile.

steps.title: •	BLOOD GROUPING
steps.instruction: A drop of a known antisera was added to the sample.

steps.title: •	BLOOD GROUPING
steps.instruction: The mixture was stirred with a swab stick and the tile was rocked forward and backward.

steps.title: •	BLOOD GROUPING
steps.instruction: The results were read macroscopically upon agglutination and in cases where the results were unclear, were read microscopically.
